incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), including Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 and R. 123-1 et seq.; beneficial-owner declarations are governed by Articles L. 561-46 and R. 561-55 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent greffe of the Tribunal de commerce for the registered office, acting through the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS); filings are submitted through the national Guichet unique managed by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation formalities submitted through the Guichet unique, requesting RCS registration and filing the beneficial-owner declaration; no separate statutory M0 form is ordinarily filed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to a SAS; the articles set the capital. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid at subscription, with the balance payable within five years after registration. Cash contributions are deposited with an authorized depositary, typically a bank or notary, and evidenced by a deposit certificate; funds are released after RCS registration. Contributions in kind are generally fully paid and require a contributions auditor unless a statutory exemption applies. The stated USD amount is an approximate conversion of the RCS registration charge and excludes the variable mandatory legal-notice publication charge, beneficial-owner filing charge, and any service-provider fees; verify current tariffs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, being the initial officers or authorized representatives of [Company], resolve that: (1) the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in the executed articles of association, and the President shall ensure that subscribed cash contributions are deposited and the deposit certificate retained; (2) the registered office is established at [full address] as stated in the articles; (3) [name] is appointed President for the term and on the conditions specified in the articles, and [name(s)] is/are appointed [Director(s), if applicable]; and (4) the President is authorized to complete Guichet unique and RCS formalities, make the beneficial-owner filing, and take all measures necessary to obtain registration. These resolutions take effect upon incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve and execute the SAS articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, where applicable, a French notary; the registered-office greffe is determined by the registered address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set the corporate name, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, share classes, governance, President appointment method, and transfer rules. Have all founders sign the articles. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS articles; use a notarial deed where required by the nature of a contribution, such as certain real-estate contributions.
required_dossiers: Final articles of association signed by all shareholders
Share-subscription schedule and contribution details
Identity and address details for shareholders and officers
Auditor reports or appointment documents where legally required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies between the articles, subscription records, and online filing. Obtain any required auditor report or notarial instrument before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a formation account, transfer at least the legally required portion of cash subscriptions, and obtain a certificate of deposit identifying the company in formation and the deposited amount. Retain proof of payment. The certificate is used in the registration filing; request release of funds after RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Signed articles or draft articles
Founder and beneficial-owner identification
Subscription and payment schedule
Proof of address and company-in-formation details required by the depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve KYC or source-of-funds requests with certified identity and payment evidence; correct deposit references and obtain a replacement certificate if the entity name or amount is inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A newspaper or authorized online legal-announcement service habilitated in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the prescribed formation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President details, and RCS registration location. Obtain the publication certificate for the Guichet unique filing.
required_dossiers: Articles of association
Required company and President particulars
Payment details for the publication charge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice and publication certificate if mandatory particulars are omitted or conflict with the articles; upload the corrected evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI national Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, with registration processed by the competent Tribunal de commerce greffe and RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation formalities, upload the signed articles and supporting documents, declare the beneficial owners, pay applicable charges, and monitor the portal for requests. Provide translations and authentication or apostille where required for foreign documents; notarization is not generally required solely because a shareholder is non-resident.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Registered-office evidence and, where relevant, occupancy authorization
Certificate of cash-capital deposit
Legal-announcement publication certificate
President's identification, non-conviction declaration, and parentage details where required
Beneficial-owner information and supporting identity documents
Auditor appointment or reports where applicable
Foreign corporate shareholder documents and powers of attorney, with required French translations and authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to portal or greffe deficiency notices by the stated deadline, upload corrected or additional evidence, and pay any balance due. Escalate a rejected formal filing through the Guichet unique support process and the competent greffe; do not commence business as a registered SAS until registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, competent tax service, and relevant social-security bodies through applicable registration channels.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN/SIRET and Kbis extract, arrange release of deposited capital, activate accounting and tax records, and complete employer and social-security registrations before hiring. Confirm VAT and corporate-tax registrations and retain the filed articles and registration evidence.
required_dossiers: RCS registration confirmation and Kbis extract
Articles and capital-deposit certificate
Bank account documentation
Employer and payroll information if staff will be hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or social-registration data with the relevant authority and retain proof of each correction; obtain professional advice if activity begins before all applicable registrations are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial operating licence or industrial licensing board applies to the described manufacturing activity. The competent prefecture and Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) oversee installations classified for environmental protection (ICPE), where applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing operating permit is required solely for producing plastic model kits. Prior ICPE declaration, registration, or environmental authorization may be required depending on the actual processes, equipment, storage, substances, and applicable ICPE nomenclature thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition; relevant processing authorities include the regional DREAL and the prefecture.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No automatic EIA classification can be determined from the stated business description alone. For an ICPE project, the applicable nomenclature and project characteristics determine whether it requires a declaration, registration, environmental authorization, or case-by-case EIA screening and, if required, a full environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single sector-specific numerical threshold applies on the supplied facts. Comply with applicable ICPE prescriptions, water-law requirements, municipal sewer discharge conditions, and air-emission limits set by the applicable classification or permit. Characterize and segregate hazardous and non-hazardous waste, use authorized waste channels, and retain tracking records where required. Assess injection-molding equipment, coating or solvent use, combustion plant, and chemical storage against the ICPE nomenclature before installation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before use, comply with building-planning and construction rules, workplace health and safety requirements, fire-prevention duties, and applicable electrical and machinery-safety standards. An establishment open to the public (ERP) requires applicable fire and accessibility approvals; an ordinary industrial workplace does not have a universal standalone fire certificate. Obtain building-owner or authority approvals for structural alterations and equipment loads, and complete workplace risk assessment and required safety inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); the official online tax portal is impots.gouv.fr. Foreign businesses without a French establishment generally deal with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SAS through the business formalities single window (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated via INPI). INSEE assigns the entity a SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET. Obtain a French VAT identification number from the competent SIE or, for a foreign business without a French establishment, the SIEE; the number is generally FR followed by a two-digit key and the SIREN. A non-EU business generally must appoint a French fiscal representative unless an applicable statutory exemption or reciprocal arrangement applies. EU businesses generally register directly without a fiscal representative. VAT registration is required before commencing taxable transactions for which French VAT is due; a foreign taxable person is not generally entitled to rely on the domestic small-business threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS), at the standard rate of 25%, subject to applicable reduced-rate conditions. A qualifying SAS may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR) for up to five fiscal years if the statutory ownership, activity, age, size, and other conditions are met. There is no US-style check-the-box election. French tax classification and hybrid-mismatch treatment are governed by French law and applicable EU rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT, taxe sur la valeur ajoutée or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For eligible French-established small businesses, the domestic VAT exemption regime generally uses annual turnover thresholds of EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and certain related activities and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory excess thresholds and activity-specific rules. These thresholds do not generally protect foreign taxable persons making taxable supplies in France; a foreign business may need to register from its first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic electronic invoicing and transaction/payment-data e-reporting through the public invoicing portal or a registered private platform. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations apply from that date to large businesses and mid-sized enterprises, and from 1 September 2027 to SMEs and micro-enterprises. E-invoicing applies to covered domestic B2B transactions between parties subject to French VAT; e-reporting applies to specified transactions outside that scope, including relevant B2C and cross-border transactions. France does not impose general real-time pre-clearance or mandatory digital stamping of every invoice. Structured data, transmission, and platform requirements apply under the phased regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with credit (effectively 0%) when statutory conditions are met and the exporter can substantiate that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate exemption, VAT-identification, reporting, and transport-evidence rules. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore; place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies, and specific exemptions may require additional conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and evidence of exit from the EU customs territory, including the export accompanying document or equivalent electronic customs confirmation
Commercial invoice and order or sales contract identifying the goods, buyer, and destination
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, carrier documentation, or proof of delivery
Evidence linking the exported goods to the customs declaration and sale, including packing list and shipment records
Foreign-exchange or inward-remittance evidence where available and relevant; a French inward remittance certificate is not a general statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The taxpayer must retain reliable evidence supporting the export exemption and comply with VAT return, invoicing, and record-retention obligations. If export or other exemption conditions are not proven, the DGFiP may assess VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable tax penalties. Intentional fraud or failure to meet reporting obligations may attract enhanced penalties and, where statutory elements are met, criminal sanctions. Input VAT deductions or refunds attributable to unsupported exempt transactions may be denied or recovered.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France’s central bank and part of the Eurosystem. The French Treasury (Direction générale du Trésor) administers relevant external-financial-relations rules. Prudential supervision of banks is principally conducted by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), within the applicable European Union framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies the euro-area framework and generally has no exchange controls restricting ordinary current-account payments or capital movements. Cross-border transfers remain subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, and statistical-reporting requirements. A SAS may generally receive foreign investment, pay foreign suppliers, and remit dividends or other lawful distributions, subject to corporate-law procedures, available distributable profits, withholding-tax rules, treaty relief documentation, and the recipient’s tax treatment. Banks may require evidence of the transaction’s commercial or corporate purpose and source of funds. Transfers involving sanctioned parties or jurisdictions may be prohibited or require authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated and no mandatory foreign-currency conversion ratio for ordinary commercial exports. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign currency or in an eligible foreign account, subject to applicable banking, sanctions, tax, accounting, and statistical-reporting obligations. The company should record export revenue and foreign-currency balances in its books and retain invoices, customs and transport evidence, and bank records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before registration, where required for subscription of share capital; operational business account after registration
Capital deposit account before registration, where available; operational business account after registration
Capital deposit account before registration, where available; operational business account after registration

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE (including Banque Populaire and Caisse d’Epargne entities)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital deposit account before registration, where available; operational business account after registration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An electronic money institution authorized in France or another EEA state and entitled to provide services in France may support payments and foreign-currency services within its authorization and product terms. It is not necessarily a deposit-taking bank, and e-money safeguarding is not equivalent to deposit-guarantee protection. Offshore providers without the required EEA authorization or passporting rights should not be treated as an assured substitute for a French corporate bank. Confirm account ownership, safeguarding, payment limits, supported currencies, client-money arrangements, and ability to process capital contributions and tax or payroll payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no general French statutory requirement that every SAS director attend a bank branch in person to open an account. Remote onboarding may be permitted, subject to the bank’s identity-verification, beneficial-owner, risk, and document-authentication standards. A bank may require an in-person or live video interview, certified or legalized documents, French translations, or additional verification, particularly for non-resident directors, complex ownership, or higher-risk payment corridors. The company should confirm onboarding requirements with the selected institution before relying on remote opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner; layered or opaque ownership; trust or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extracts and constitutional documents for each ownership layer; ownership chart identifying natural-person beneficial owners; identity and address evidence; beneficial-owner filings; explanation of control and economic rationale; certified translations or legalization where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, unusually large initial funding, or transfers from an account not held in the investor’s name
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription and corporate resolutions; investor bank statements; audited accounts, tax returns, sale agreements, or other source-of-wealth evidence; proof of the originating account’s ownership; transfer instruction identifying the investor and the SAS; explanation of any third-party funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk, sanctioned, or geographically inconsistent counterparties, or payment narratives inconsistent with the company’s stated activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty identity and beneficial-owner records; sanctions-screening results; signed contracts, purchase orders, invoices, shipping and customs documents; explanation of the commercial relationship and payment route; evidence that no restricted party or prohibited transaction is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Manufacturing activity, steel or plastics sourcing, imports, or export flows not supported by a coherent operating profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan and forecast; supplier and customer contracts; product descriptions and applicable commodity classifications; premises or manufacturing arrangements; customs, transport, and insurance records; tax and VAT registrations where applicable; projected payment volumes and currencies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unrelated third parties, cash, or multiple intermediaries to fund or settle company transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and payment-control procedures; explanation and documentary trail for any exceptional transfer; evidence of company-account ownership; reconciliations linking each transfer to an invoice, capital contribution, or approved distribution; remediation plan discontinuing unsupported routing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a pre-registration share subscription, use a bank or other legally eligible capital-deposit provider and obtain the deposit certificate required for incorporation; funds are released or transferred in accordance with the applicable incorporation process. After registration, route additional equity or shareholder financing to an account held in the SAS’s name, with the legal nature documented as a capital increase, share premium, or shareholder loan. Instruct the sending bank to identify the investor, beneficiary SAS, currency, and precise transaction purpose; use an accurate narrative such as share subscription, capital increase, or shareholder loan rather than an invented or generic regulatory purpose code. Retain subscription documents, corporate approvals, registration evidence, source-of-funds records, and the incoming payment confirmation. France does not generally impose a universal FX purpose-code system for these transfers, but banks may request supporting documents and apply reporting, sanctions, and AML controls. Confirm any applicable statistical-reporting treatment with the bank or Banque de France reporting guidance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settle supplier invoices through SEPA credit transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT cross-border transfers, including MT103 customer-credit-transfer messaging where applicable, for other currencies or corridors. Match beneficiary details, invoice currency, contract terms, and payment references; retain invoices, purchase orders, shipping and customs records, and proof of delivery. Commercial documentary credits may be issued through a bank using applicable documentary-credit rules, commonly UCP 600, subject to credit approval, fees, and collateral. For foreign-currency payments, document the underlying exposure and agree exchange-rate execution, value date, fees, and any intermediary-bank charges with the bank. Screen beneficiaries and relevant banks against applicable EU and French sanctions restrictions before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or other eligible counterparty, generally supported by an identifiable commercial exposure and subject to counterparty documentation, collateral terms, and applicable financial-market rules.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered and legally available for the relevant currency and counterparty; settlement, product classification, reporting, and clearing obligations must be assessed under applicable EU rules.
Currency swaps and FX swaps with eligible counterparties for documented liquidity or hedging needs, subject to contractual, collateral, reporting, and applicable EMIR requirements.
Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion of receipts and payments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, potential daily penalty, director liability, and possible administrative removal from the Trade and Companies Register after formal notice; no automatic statutory strike-off solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the Guichet Unique or INPI filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine generally EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; court injunction and daily penalty may apply. Persistent non-compliance may support administrative removal from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and related tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; electronic filing required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally 0.20% per month and tax surcharge generally 10%; surcharge may increase to 40% after formal notice and 80% in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the Guichet Unique or INPI filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general annual confirmation is required; file within 30 days after formation or any change in beneficial ownership or control information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential criminal penalties for the legal representative, including a fine of up to EUR 7,500 and imprisonment of up to six months; restrictions on registry formalities may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: No general annual return or franchise-tax renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable; France has no general annual corporate return or annual franchise tax for an SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not applicable; maintain ongoing registry, accounting, tax, beneficial-owner, and corporate-record obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is assessed against the specific missed filing or record-maintenance obligation rather than against a general annual-return requirement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or an average of 50 employees. Additional mandatory-audit rules may apply to certain groups, controlled entities, or qualifying ownership structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations for statutory standalone accounts. IFRS is generally used for qualifying consolidated accounts and may apply where legally permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a general annual UBO confirmation. The SAS must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file an amendment within 30 days after any change. Share transfers require updating the shareholder accounts and the register of movements of securities; the articles of association may impose additional approval or transfer restrictions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or shareholder accounts
Register of directors and corporate officers
Minute book or electronic record of shareholder and management decisions
Beneficial-owner information record and filed declaration

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,000 per year for commercial domiciliation or registered-office services; France does not generally require a separate annual registered-agent fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-10,000 per year for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; complex groups and larger operations may materially exceed this range.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) filed via impots.gouv.fr EDI-TDFC/efi; includes supplementary 2058-A
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for 31 Dec year-end, e-filing deadline is 3 May of following year
